#5189. Riot Liquidates 79% of Its Bitcoin Treasury for $28 Billion AI Infrastructure Deal

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

American Riot Platforms Inc. (RIOT) sold off 79% of its Bitcoin in the third quarter of 2026, redirecting capital toward building infrastructure for artificial intelligence. According to a fresh financial report, the company reduced its cryptocurrency reserves from 11,380 to 2,418 BTC.

In total, over the first nine months of the year, Riot sold 20,264 BTC on the market, receiving about $1.5 billion for them. This money went toward financing a major technological shift: the company's free energy capacity is being repurposed for high-performance computing needs.

Riot shares reacted to the session open with a sharp jump to $16.20, after which they stabilized in the $15.45–$15.50 range, holding positions on elevated volumes.

The main incentive for selling the cryptocurrency was a 15-year agreement to lease ready-made sites and capacities (powered land lease) totaling 910 MW at the Corsicana campus in Texas. The strategic partner was the Frontier AI Lab (Anthropic) laboratory.

The initial cost of the contract is estimated at $28 billion, and the average annual rent at the start will be about $1.8 billion. Taking into account other projects, Riot's total long-term revenue in the data center segment has reached $38 billion, and the total controlled capacity is 1,151 MW.

Riot CEO Jason Les noted that the agreement is structured as a triple-net lease. Under its terms, the client itself purchases and maintains the computing equipment. For Riot, this reduces construction costs by roughly half compared to standard Tier 3 data centers. As a result, the company will be able to do without issuing new shares and diluting investors' stakes.

The shift in focus is occurring against the backdrop of falling margins in classic mining. Riot's quarterly revenue from cryptocurrency mining fell by 28% — to $116 million, although the company actually mined 1,637 BTC.

Nevertheless, total quarterly revenue held at $181.4 million (+1% year-over-year), outpacing market forecasts. Net profit amounted to $4.03 million.

To optimize its balance sheet, the company fully closed its $200 million credit line with Coinbase, returning 5,821 BTC from collateral. Riot ended the quarter with free liquidity of $950.2 million (including cash and the remainder of the cryptocurrency). The balance sheet retains 2,418 BTC, which may also go under the hammer in the fourth quarter to finance the Texas construction.

#5187. Five Ways North Korea Breaks Into Crypto Firms—and How Binance Was Hacked

Five Ways North Korea Breaks Into Crypto Firms—and How Binance Was Hacked

Hackers from North Korea are notoriously effective at stealing crypto, with one estimate attributing 60% of all losses last year to DPRK-linked groups. These hackers enlist several different vectors of attack, making it all the more difficult to spot them in the act.

Last week, it took just 20 minutes for alleged North Korean hackers to drain $6.3 billion from Binance, in what is the biggest crypto hack on record. The attackers compromised a Binance engineer's work computer through a fake job interview, used an internal AI tool to gain control of other engineers' computers, and then used stolen credentials to hijack an internal wallet signing service, the exchange said.

In the past, North Korean hackers have been known to get hired at crypto companies under fake identities, attack through third-party infrastructure, and poison widely used code libraries. More recently, they've started using AI to make all of it more convincing.

Here are some examples of the methods that North Korean hackers are known to use in crypto attacks.

Binance chief security officer Jimmy Su told Decrypt in August 2025 that the exchange throws out suspected North Korean resumes every day, and that "almost all the large DPRK hacks," at the time, had involved a fake employee helping facilitate the attack.

Su said there were tell-tale signs in resumes that indicate the applicant was from North Korea, but the exchange was not willing to reveal the specifics on the red flags. Sometimes, though, malicious actors get through to the interview stage, where the attackers use deepfakes to change their face and voice.

"The only real good detection is that they almost always have a slow internet connection," he told Decrypt. "What's happening is that the translation and the voice changer are working during the call … that's why they are always delayed."

Those who do get hired tend to be suspiciously good at the job. Su said North Korean workers are often among a company's top performers, likely because several people may be sharing one role across time zones.

The threat has not let up. Binance said its security team detected and prevented 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyber threat cases in 2026, using techniques ranging from fraudulent job interviews to fake video conferencing apps.

Attackers also flip the scam around and pose as recruiters to target people who already work at high-profile crypto companies. Often, the attacker will claim there's a video or audio issue during the interview and send the victim a link to update Zoom, which infects their device with malware

"The DPRK group will [also] try to schedule calls with the external-facing employees," Su told Decrypt. "Either as a DeFi project or investment firm. Worst yet, they'll be recruiting them for a high-level job, paying twice, three times as much, just to get them onto an interview."

This is how the Binance attack began, according to the exchange. In September, a Binance software engineer was approached through a legitimate job-hunting platform by someone posing as a project director, who set up two interviews. In the first, a purported HR representative built trust over a live video call by sharing a social media account full of personal photos and videos, an approach Binance called "more advanced and deceptive than previously seen."

In the second, held on a chat app, the engineer was told to download an "assignment" onto his work computer. The code repository contained previously unknown malware that ran during setup, swapped a legitimate developer tool for a malicious version and connected to an attacker-controlled server, evading Binance's security tools.

One North Korea-linked group infected at least 30,000 devices in more than 100 countries between roughly December 2025 and July 2026 using similar methods. It took funds or credentials from more than 7,000 crypto wallets and moved around $10.71 million to North Korea.

The group, known as WaterPlum or Contagious Interview, posed as AI, crypto, or NFT companies and set candidates a technical interview or coding task that required downloading malware-filled files. Some used AI face-swapping software during interviews before cutting their video and asking the candidate to do the same, blaming a bad connection.

Binance's Su also told Decrypt that North Korean hackers poison public code libraries, ranking it as the second most common method of attack—behind fake employees.

Node Package Manager (NPM) packages are collections of reusable, open-source code that developers frequently use. Attackers can clone these packages and slip in a small line of malicious code while keeping its original function. That means that a victim could use this poisoned code library and not notice, with the malicious code embedding itself deeper over time as more is built on top of it.

In September 2025, software security firm ReversingLabs found two NPM packages that used Ethereum smart contracts to download malware, which the firm said it hadn't seen before. The packages were tied to a wider network of GitHub repositories, mostly branded as crypto trading bots, with thousands of commits and stars that ReversingLabs thinks were mostly faked.

The tactic formed part of a “sophisticated campaign” of malicious actors attempting to hack users via poisoned blockchain-related public code libraries, a vector of attack that Binance has previously attributed to North Korean hackers.

To counter the threat, Su said, Binance makes employees go through NPM libraries with a fine-tooth comb.

Tampered developer tools also played a part in the Binance hack. In June, a member of Binance's wallet DevOps team downloaded a tampered installation of Homebrew, a popular software installer, while trying to install an AI coding tool he had found through a search engine, the exchange said. Its security team caught the problem, replaced the device and rotated his credentials, but the incident exposed the engineer and his colleagues on the wallet infrastructure team to the attackers.

Before Binance, the unwanted record for the largest crypto hack belonged to Bybit, which lost $1.4 billion in February 2025. Cybersecurity firms revealed that North Korean hackers pulled off the attack by planting malicious code into the infrastructure of Safe—a crypto wallet provider used by the exchange.

The security firms said malicious JavaScript code was directly injected into Safe's online infrastructure. Though, it was unclear how the attackers managed to do this.

Bybit's infrastructure "was not compromised," the exchange told Decrypt, and the hack came purely because a third party was exploited.

The Binance attack targeted the exchange's own systems. On October 29, the attacker used stolen credentials to deploy a container and gain unauthorized access to an internal wallet signing service, which let it initiate transactions outside Binance's normal withdrawal process. On Ethereum, it used the signing service to exploit EIP-7702, a mechanism that lets an account delegate execution rights to a smart contract, giving an attacker-controlled contract partial control over a Binance hot wallet.

Those on-chain authorizations kept working even after Binance suspended withdrawals. Because the hot wallet used multi-party computation, there was no single private key Binance could use to revoke them quickly, the exchange said.

Every single one of the above mentioned attack vectors can be turbo-charged with artificial intelligence tools.

Early this year, Google warned of an AI-powered malware campaign targeting crypto companies coming from North Korea. Similarly, Binance's Su also mentioned that AI tools can be used to increase the effectiveness of attacks.

Concerns around AI-powered hacks have risen in recent months, with Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin saying in October that it's "plausible" AI could break encryption within the next two years. It came amid an explosion in AI-driven maths, with OpenAI claiming to have cracked a 90-year-old maths problem in a matter of days. Experts urged the industry to prepare for AI-powered attacks on encryption.

There are no confirmed reports of North Korean hackers using AI to break encryption. But given how quickly they've adopted AI elsewhere, the industry may have to prepare for that next.

#5186. XRP Ledger Activates New Amendment to Strengthen Network

The XRP Ledger (XRPL) network recently activated a new amendment that helps secure the network by resolving potential security weaknesses and making some existing functionalities more robust and reliable.

This latest amendment, called fixCleanup3_4_0, was activated on Nov. 4, bringing a series of technical updates that include fixes for token issuance, automated market makers (AMMs), lending functionalities, and other parts of the XRP Ledger network.

A fix for a potential security weak point related to token issuance on the XRP Ledger network is a critical aspect of the latest amendment.

As explained in the official documentation of the XRP Ledger network, this update addresses a potential weakness related to delegated permissions that could allow some accounts to issue tokens when they are only allowed to destroy them.

On the XRP Ledger, token issuers can grant permissions to other accounts to perform certain tasks. For example, a stablecoin issuer could delegate permission to burn tokens to another account when customers want to redeem them.

With the latest amendment, the XRP Ledger network addresses this security weakness by preventing a zero-balance, burn-only delegated payment from resulting in the issuance of new tokens.

On top of addressing token issuance permissions, there's more to the fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment.

As explained in the official XRP Ledger network documentation, the fixCleanup3_4_0 update brings several fixes to decentralized trading, asset management, and transaction processing.

For automated market makers (AMMs), this latest update prevents some invalid auction bids and makes some improvements to how liquidity withdrawals and token clawbacks work.

It also brings some fixes for potential unexpected calculation errors or rounding issues that could occur in some cases.

These changes are supposed to make things more predictable when it comes to liquidity pools and avoid potential failures that could happen in some cases.

Another significant aspect of these changes concerns Single Asset Vaults and the proposed native lending infrastructure on the XRP Ledger.

As explained, this amendment brings some improvements to how rounding is handled when assets enter or exit vaults.

The idea is to ensure that transactions do not result in more or fewer assets being transferred than they should.

#5183. Ripple Executive Reveals Massive Growth of Company's London Hub

According to Ripple's UK and Europe Managing Director, Cassie Craddock, Ripple’s London office has expanded significantly over the last decade to become Ripple’s largest international hub outside the U.S.

“When we moved into our current office in 2018, there were 2 floors, and a lot of empty desks. Now we’re on 3 floors and full on all the desks. We’re now over capacity,” she wrote on X.

Craddock's comments came after she took part in a fireside chat at the British Residence in New York as part of Ripple’s Swell conference.

She revealed that Ripple chose to focus on London early on, given the UK's strong capital markets, mature legal system, experienced regulators and concentration of financial talent.

However, she added that regulatory uncertainty had previously limited the company’s capacity to build more relationships with leading U.K. financial institutions.

Ripple's story in the U.K. capital began on March 21, 2016, when the San Francisco-based company officially announced the launch of its first office in London, located in Canary Wharf.

Back then, the expansion was meant to accommodate the growing interest of European banks in distributed ledger technology and cross-border settlement solutions.

Ripple incorporated its U.K. entity in April 2016 under the name Ripple Europe Ltd. (later changed to Ripple Markets UK Ltd. in August 2022).

Ripple continued to expand its ties to U.K. financial institutions in the following years.

In April 2018, Santander introduced its new international payments app, One Pay FX, which used Ripple’s xCurrent technology.

In February 2022, Ripple announced a partnership with London-based payments company Modulr to make it easier to send cross-border payments to the UK and Europe.

Moreover, Ripple has played a role in developing the research landscape for blockchain in the U.K. In January 2026, Ripple shared that it had pledged more than £5M to UK universities under its University Blockchain Research Initiative.

One of the major milestones for Ripple in the U.K. occurred on Jan. 9, when Ripple received an Electronic Money Institution license and cryptoasset registration from the Financial Conduct Authority. The authorizations enabled Ripple to extend its regulated cross-border payment services to UK institutions.

In February, Ripple also secured a partnership with Aviva Investors to explore the tokenization of traditional investment funds.

This work resulted in the launch of a tokenized share class of Aviva Investors’ £22bn Sterling Liquidity Fund on the XRP Ledger on Oct. 26.

#5182. Morgan Stanley Starts Tokenizing US Stocks and Treasuries via DTCC

Home » Crypto Market News » Morgan Stanley Starts Tokenizing US Stocks and Treasuries via DTCC

The bank confirmed it is among the first financial institutions to adopt DTCC’s tokenization service.

Morgan Stanley is taking a major step into modern market infrastructure by tokenizing U.S. equities and Treasuries through the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation’s (DTCC) new Tokenization Service (DTS).

Following the platform’s official launch on October 28, the bank confirmed on X that it is actively using the system to create digital representations of traditional real-world assets.

This move brings Wall Street’s largest institutions closer to fully digital, on-chain trading infrastructure. More than 20 major financial firms—including JPMorgan and Citi—have signed agreements to participate

In its official X post, Morgan Stanley said it is “among the first banks to tokenize real-world assets” following the DTS launch. The bank said the service converts US equities and US Treasurys into tokenized form.

We are thrilled to announce that Morgan Stanley is among the first banks to tokenize real-world assets following the launch of the @The_DTCC Tokenization Service (DTS), converting U.S. Equity and U.S. Treasuries to tokenized form. Launched on October 28, DTS creates tokenized… pic.twitter.com/wUNMnYB5gC

According to the announcement, DTS creates tokenized representations of securities held in custody at the Depository Trust Company (DTC). Morgan Stanley said the goal is greater liquidity, collateral mobility, and capital efficiency.

DTS has been live since October 28 on the Canton Network and Hyperledger Besu blockchain. The service initially supports selected companies in the Russell 1000 index, ETFs tracking major indices, and US Treasury bills, notes, and bonds. The tokenized assets are designed to support 24/7 settlement, liquidity, and use as collateral.

According to DTCC, approximately $30 trillion in eligible securities may be covered by the initial rollout. More than 20 firms, including JPMorgan and Citi, have signed on to the service.

The tokenized real-world asset (RWA) market is worth $39.4 billion, with U.S. Treasuries accounting for more than $14.2 billion, according to RWA.xyz.

This institutional migration onto blockchain rails is made possible by clear regulatory framework updates. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) issued a no-action letter to the DTCC, allowing its subsidiary DTC to operate tokenization services on approved blockchains under a three-year framework.

The SEC also approved rule updates allowing Nasdaq to roll out tokenized settlement options for Russell 1000 equities and major index-tracking ETFs, while work continues on broader digital asset innovation standards.

As the central backbone of U.S. market clearing, the DTCC oversees more than $114 trillion in assets under custody. Its adoption of public-enterprise hybrid blockchains marks a decisive shift from experimental pilot programs to fully regulated, mainstream financial operations.

#5179. Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX Block Their Stock From OKX-ICE Tokenized Venue

Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX Block Their Stock From OKX-ICE Tokenized Venue

Two of Elon Musk’s companies are now keeping their shares off OKX and ICE’s planned tokenized stock venue.

Tesla and SpaceX are among six new objecting issuers listed in an updated notice from OKXICE TSV dated Monday. Amazon, Netflix, Lam Research, and SoFi Technologies are the others. The additions bring the total to 56 companies.

The list stood at 50 in the venue’s Oct. 30 notice, when Nvidia, Costco, and Nike led the biggest batch yet. That followed 38 on Oct. 28, after Walmart joined, and nine on Oct. 15, when the first objectors appeared.

The new names deepen the roster of megacap holdouts. Amazon, Tesla, and Netflix join Microsoft, Alphabet, and Nvidia, while SoFi, a fintech company that offers crypto trading, adds a company with its own stake in digital assets. SpaceX, which trades under the ticker SPCX, rounds out the batch.

Under the SEC’s innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate, a venue must notify a company before offering a version of its shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party.

If the company objects in writing within 30 days, the venue can’t make that stock available for trading, according to the SEC’s order. The objection applies only to that venue.

OKXICE TSV, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX’s U.S. holding company, plans to offer tokenized U.S. stocks 24/7 through permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC.

To trade, users must pass identity and sanctions checks and hold a nontransferable “soulbound” token that the venue’s smart contracts verify before every transaction.

Apple is now one of the few megacap names still missing from the list. And while objections bar OKXICE from listing third-party tokenized versions of a company’s stock, they don’t close every door.

The notice says the venue can also list shares tokenized by the issuers themselves, though it doesn’t identify any, and that tokenized stocks it offers aren’t restricted to trading on OKXICE alone.

#5178. Weekend stock tokens predict Monday open, but guessing up scores 55%

Bitquery’s pre-futures weekend test found no clear directional edge, while Nasdaq’s proposed weekday expansion remains conditional.

Stock tokens kept trading through weekends, but their prices did not reliably guide the next stock-market open in a new study of 121 stocks.

Blockchain data provider Bitquery's Nov. 3 analysis found that Sunday token moves measured before equity-index futures reopened correctly called 54% of qualifying openings, so simply predicting that every stock would open higher scored 55%.

More hours can give investors another opportunity to transact, but they do not show that the resulting prices predict the next opening better.

Bitquery followed 17 weekends beginning July 10 through Oct. 30, with the final stock opening on Nov. 2. It recorded 791 stock-opening observations across those stocks, and its direction test kept the 533 openings that moved at least 0.5% from Friday's close.

Token moves pointed the right way on 286 of those observations, compared with 291 correct calls for always predicting a rise. Because more openings rose than fell, a 50% coin-toss benchmark alone would flatter the tokens' result.

The study also used balanced accuracy, which averages success on rises and falls. The tokens scored 53%, with a reported 95% interval of 44% to 62%.

Across all 791 observations, including smaller moves, the median error was 1.2% using token moves versus 0.9% assuming the stock opened at Friday's close. Bitquery put the excess error at 0.3%, with a 95% range of 0.2% to 0.5%.

Bitquery's study asks different questions about direction and forecast size. The later Sunday reading also changes the information and the sample.

The main direction test ends just before futures reopen. It filters on the stock's opening move.

The later check follows futures reopening and changes both liquidity and movement filters.

Trading access and useful forecasting information remain separate claims.

Vendor research, not independent raw-data replication. No futures-price benchmark or cost-adjusted strategy. The later cutoff, volume floor and movement filter change together.

Reported study figures only. Main test: 17 weekends beginning July 10–October 30, openings through November 2. Direction filters stock moves below 0.5%; size uses all 791 observations. Panel intervals are reported 95% ranges. Point and interval geometry maps linearly onto the same 40%–70% balanced-accuracy scale; this is an interval plot, not a zero-based bar chart.

Vendor research, not independent raw-data replication. No futures-price benchmark or cost-adjusted strategy. The later cutoff, volume floor and movement filter change together.

The main test read token prices just before 6 p.m. Sunday ET, the futures reopening cutoff used by Bitquery. That timing is important because a later token price could incorporate information already available from equity-index futures.

A separate check using prices just before 8 p.m. returned 59% balanced accuracy, with a 95% range of 53% to 65%, across 220 openings. But it also raised the weekend-volume threshold to $1 million and changed the movement filter.

Listings needed at least $10,000 of weekend trading and a trade in the hour before each cutoff. The study excluded openings affected by stock splits or ex-dividend dates and crypto-sensitive stocks such as Strategy and Coinbase, then combined issuers using weekend-volume weights.

Earlier perpetual-market research reported improved forecasts from final weekend prices in a different sample. Different instruments, liquidity filters and observation times prevent that result from serving as a direct rebuttal to this test.

Nasdaq's Oct. 30 update described Dec. 6 as the expected transition to 23-hour, five-day trading, subject to clearing and market-data infrastructure being ready. Its related market-data proposals also remain subject to regulatory approval.

Its member implementation notice describes an added 9 p.m. to 4 a.m. ET session requiring new member ports.

If the rollout proceeds, wider conventional weekday hours would narrow one stock-token advantage for investors whose brokers and jurisdictions permit both routes. Weekend trading and the ability to hold tokens in a blockchain wallet remain separate benefits to assess.

For example, Kraken's xStocks disclosure excludes the US, Canada, UK and Australia, permits compatible-wallet withdrawals and says holders lack ownership and voting rights in the underlying shares.

The next useful evidence would hold timing and eligibility constant, compare against available market benchmarks, and measure executable results after costs. Until then, an available weekend price should not be mistaken for a demonstrated forecasting advantage.

#5177. Binance's CZ Sounds Alarm Over New Crypto Phishing Scam

Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) has warned about a malicious crypto phishing scheme that uses a fake Trust Wallet website to lure unsuspecting users into connecting their wallets.

CZ shared a warning about a fraudulent website with a fake domain that mimics the popular Trust Wallet website.

Attackers modified the website domain by replacing the “u” with “a” and changing the extension from “.com” to “.cam,” which may trick unsuspecting users who don’t carefully inspect the domain.

The malicious website tricks users into connecting their crypto wallets in order to review their transfers.

However, the site contains JavaScript code that attempts to scan wallet balances using a backend API in order to prepare transfers to specific wallet addresses.

The attacker’s setup works with multiple well-known crypto wallets such as Trust Wallet, Phantom, and OKX Wallet.

CZ’s warning comes shortly after a surge in crypto phishing attempts against wallet users.

On Nov. 3, cybersecurity firm Bitdefender announced that scammers had started using the recent Binance security breach to spread fake emails impersonating Trust Wallet.

The phishing emails suggested that Trust Wallet users were also impacted by the Binance security breach. Therefore, they instructed users to perform a mandatory wallet verification procedure.

The email messages warned that users would be suspended after Nov. 7 if they did not complete the wallet verification process.

Bitdefender said that the phishing scheme affected users in multiple countries, including the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Ireland and South Africa.

The phishing messages led users to fake verification websites where their wallet credentials or recovery data could be leaked.

Earlier this year, cybersecurity analysts from CYFIRMA spotted another phishing attack against Trust Wallet users. The attackers used malicious QR codes on Telegram to target Trust Wallet users.

#5175. Zcash targets 67% shorter block times – Can ZEC overcome funding uncertainty?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Zcash [ZEC] is preparing a major network upgrade that will reduce block time. The network upgrade (NU7) is designed to shorten the time it takes for blocks to be processed.

Set to be implemented on the 6th of November, this new system will enable Zcash to decrease block processing times by approximately 67%, from 75 seconds to 25 seconds.

Simply, the direct result of this change will likely be the ability for users to finalize transactions significantly faster than before. In addition, it will enable the network to process more total activity, all without altering the amount of ZEC that is added to circulation each day.

Notably, there are two other aspects of the upgrade in need of attention. First, the Sprout pool will no longer exist. Second, 60% of every transaction fee collected by the network will now go into a deferred reserve.

However, how successful these upgrades are in creating the desired effect will depend on whether the faster confirmation rates create increased adoption on-chain.

Although NU7 improves the way Zcash’s network operates, the Zcash funding model faces a separate challenge.

Who gets to control the future funding for development was a subject of debate for weeks prior to the 3rd of November. This was when Zcash Community Grants announced that it had withdrawn its proposal to direct about 98,000 ZEC into future miner rewards.

Notably, that amount represented about half of its entire treasury.

The proposal would have drawn 36,200 ZEC from ZCG’s 91,500-ZEC treasury, with the remainder coming from reduced future allocations through 2028. However, its withdrawal leaves the original funding structure intact.

As such, ZCG will continue receiving 8% of newly issued ZEC, equivalent to roughly 144 ZEC daily. Miners retain 80%, while 12% enters the coinholder-controlled lockbox.

Although withdrawing the proposal leaves current distributions intact, alternative proposals continue to leave long-term funding for development uncertain.

Beyond governance uncertainty, Zcash’s institutional demand also shows signs of weakening, although recent flows suggest a possible shift. ZEC spot ETFs recorded three consecutive days of withdrawals, with weekly net outflows reaching $7.21 million.

However, the 4th of November saw a $3.43 million inflow into ZEC spot ETFs, ending the streak of net outflows. The inflow increased total cumulative net inflows to $217.73 million and net assets to $756.83 million. Volume also hit $59.45 million.

While there was an increase in net inflows recently, recent outflows indicate that institutions become more cautious. Additionally, while ETFs still hold 3.43% of outstanding circulation of ZEC, institutions do maintain a significant presence in spite of decreased demand.

#5174. French bank resumes transfers after $133 million attack but leaves crypto loss unconfirmed

Arkéa says attackers used its own account through a provider's platform, while a separate $108.8 million USDC trail leaves the bank-to-crypto link unproven.

French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said almost all operations had resumed on Nov. 4 after an attack enabled fraudulent crypto transactions from its own account, delaying some customer transfers.

In a later clarification, the bank said attackers reached it through a service provider's platform and sent money to other banks. Those transactions may then have enabled conversion into cryptocurrency through specialized platforms.

Arkéa did not confirm that conversion or connect its transfers to specific crypto wallets.

The bank denied that the attack entered through Fortuneo, its online banking subsidiary, and said it did not use customer accounts. It described the incident as contained and said customers' holdings were unaffected.

Arkéa declined to confirm whether €118 million ($133 million) had been stolen and validated only their order of magnitude. It said some funds had been blocked and further recovery efforts were underway, making a definitive financial amount premature.

The amount involved in fraudulent transactions is not necessarily the bank's final loss once blocked funds and recoveries are accounted for. Arkéa said the sums would not threaten its financial strength.

Its initial statement described precautionary transaction suspensions and a gradual restart after checks and stronger security measures. The later update said almost all operations had resumed during the morning.

Arkéa said it was working with judicial and police authorities to determine the attack's origin and method.

Separately, blockchain analytics firm Bitquery reported tracing $108.8 million in USDC withdrawals from wallets it labels as belonging to Kraken, Crypto.com and OKX to 15 addresses on Nov. 1 and 2. The withdrawals ran from 12:25 UTC on Nov. 1 to 09:09 UTC the next day, roughly 21 hours.

Bitquery said it cannot see bank transfers or exchange accounts, so the transactions cannot independently establish the alleged route from Arkéa into crypto or identify the owners of the receiving accounts.

Brazil's largest crypto exchange says its users won't pay for its hack. Mercado Bitcoin, which lost tens of millions of dollars on Monday, says the losses are its problem, not its customers'.

An exchange holds your coins the way a bank holds your cash, and when one gets robbed, the customers are often the ones left waiting to see what they get back.

The exchange spotted a breach early on November 2 and froze deposits and withdrawals. “We identified and quickly contained a security incident in one of our systems early this morning,” Mercado Bitcoin said in a Portuguese-language statement on X. “As a preventive protection measure, deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended.”

It said no customer lost money and no data leaked. It has not said how the attackers got in.

How much was taken depends on who is counting. Security firm Hypernative flagged more than $40 million in suspicious transfers across at least 10 blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and Tron.

The exchange's own number is lower. “Right now the value of the assets involved is about $38 million,” Mercado Bitcoin said in a Portuguese-language update on X. “After a quick action with the crypto community and strategic partners, including Tether, Circle, Paxos, BRL1 and Chainalysis, we have already blocked $11 million.”

Others put it higher. Blockchain analysts at Arkham traced at least $46 million, while Chainalysis says about $49 million, with nearly $10 million frozen. The exchange has not said whether its $38 million includes the frozen amount.

Tether, which issues the USDT stablecoin (a token pegged to the dollar), froze more than $4.5 million in USDT tied to the incident, CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X.

A freeze only stops the tokens from moving. It doesn't return them to their owner, which is why the exchange's promise to cover losses carries the weight here.

On October 29, hackers drained more than $6 billion from Binance, the world's biggest exchange, and the FBI blamed North Korea's TraderTraitor group. Mercado Bitcoin has not linked its incident to that attack.

Binance made the same pledge as Mercado Bitcoin. “Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users,” CEO Richard Teng wrote on X, adding that about 95% of the affected assets had been replenished.

Neither promise can be checked from the outside. A guarantee to cover losses is only as good as the money behind it, and exchanges don't have to show customers their books.

For now, Mercado Bitcoin deposits and withdrawals remain suspended with no restart date. The exchange says it will post updates on X and resume service once full security is restored.

Polygon developers now propose a step that has long been considered an absolute taboo in the crypto industry. They put to a vote a plan to rescue Binance and Polymarket money, and this plan is, to say it mildly, radical — zero out the hackers’ wallets at the protocol level. Ongoing cybersecurity crisis shows no signs of stopping, and now the industry is being faced with an uncomfortable choice: save systemic players or protect the inviolability of Web3’s main rule that transactions cannot be reversed. The Polygon PoS hard fork involves seizing 70.49 million POL tokens ($6.5 million at the time of the attack) from the hacker addresses to return them to the victims.

The crisis unfolded at the end of October after two independent hacks. The stolen assets were scattered across five wallets (23.86 million POL was taken from Polymarket, 46.63 million from Binance). Yes, Polygon validators immediately blacklisted the addresses, cutting off the outflow, but this is just an attempt to hold back the dam with bare hands. Manual blocking is a temporary plug, and the authors of the proposal openly admit it.

The hacker is not giving up either and is continuously bombarding the network with transactions carrying wild fees of up to 219,000 POL, counting on automation or a validator with a weakness for easy money to let the operation through for a windfall profit. Things have gone as far as direct attempts to bribe validators with cash, and the hacker simply ignored on-chain negotiations. The developers’ logic is simple: keeping millions in a manual “ban” forever is a dead end that leaves the entire network under constant fire.

No one has access to the hacker’s private keys, so Polygon is changing the consensus rules themselves. Should the hard fork get approval at a certain block, the hackers’ balances will be zeroed out, and an equivalent amount will be mirror-credited to verified Binance and Polymarket wallets — without any token printing.

Polygon Labs is well aware that such an administrative step completely negates the very idea of decentralization.

This plan inevitably triggers a strong sense of the notorious The DAO hard fork of 2016. Back then, to save the young Ethereum ecosystem, developers also had to go through a painful split of the community and ignore the “Code is Law” principle. But Polygon Labs hopes that in their case consensus among validators is already rock-solid, so they are narrowing the framework of the precedent as much as possible, positioning the fork as an exclusively one-time action.

The fate of the millions in POL token is being decided right now in a community vote. The largest validators are already in favor, since both platforms are critically important to Polygon’s survival. If the plan is approved, the software will be released after two weeks of testing, and exchanges and node operators will have to urgently update. Those who refuse to switch to the new code face automatic isolation on the old branch of the blockchain — with no connection to the main network.

#5170. Hong Kong forces crypto providers to track customer trades

Hong Kong passed its crypto tax-reporting bill, putting provider data collection in 2027 before CARF exchanges in 2028.

Hong Kong's Legislative Council passed a crypto tax-information reporting bill on Nov. 4, requiring covered providers to begin collecting information in 2027 before the Inland Revenue Department starts exchanging it with partner jurisdictions in 2028.

The department's implementation background specifies Jan. 1, 2027, for the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). Providers collect and report information to the tax authority, and the department conducts the international exchanges.

The first collection year comes before the cross-border sharing date for covered firms.

CARF establishes due diligence and annual reporting requirements for crypto-asset service providers. It concerns tax transparency, with providers gathering information that tax authorities can use, rather than setting an individual user's tax bill.

The bill also implements the amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS) for financial account information. The government says that the revised standard takes effect in 2028, with exchanges starting in 2029. Its schedule is separate from CARF's 2027 collection and 2028 exchange timetable.

One bill, two reporting calendars. Follow the information from covered providers to tax authorities.

Providers identify reportable users, collect the required information and report annually to the tax authority.

The Inland Revenue Department exchanges CARF information with partner jurisdictions; providers do not conduct that cross-border step.

Covered providers collect CARF information in 2027. The tax department begins international exchanges in 2028.

Announced future schedules, not exact exchange or domestic filing dates. Obligations depend on provider scope.

Year-aligned schedule and a selectable information-route diagram built from the official passage announcement and IRD background. No elapsed-time or filing-deadline calculation is implied.

Announced future schedules, not exact exchange or domestic filing dates. Obligations depend on provider scope.

In December 2024, Hong Kong intended to complete legislative amendments by 2026 and begin crypto-information exchanges in 2028. The Nov. 4 vote marks the legislative milestone ahead of the collection year.

In its CARF explanation, the Inland Revenue Department describes reporting providers as businesses carrying out customer exchanges between crypto-assets and fiat currencies, or between crypto-assets.

These include businesses acting as counterparties or intermediaries and those operating trading platforms. Obligations depend on the provider's connection to a jurisdiction under the framework's nexus rules.

The department describes reportable users, and relevant controlling persons of entity users, by tax residence in reportable jurisdictions. A provider must identify the relevant users or controlling persons before it can prepare information for the annual reporting process described by the department.

Its explanation lists identifying details, tax-residence information, and aggregated transaction information among the required data. That scope is key when assessing a provider's obligations and which customers' information is reportable.

Hong Kong says exchanges will be reciprocal and subject to confidentiality and security safeguards. The Inland Revenue Department will issue guidance and has established a dedicated team to provide technical support and answer industry inquiries.

The department also says it will develop a CARF reporting portal and publish the data schema that defines the reporting format, with further details to follow. Those materials will set out more of the reporting process for providers preparing to collect the required data in 2027.

Bitcoin rallied as Democrats took Congress, yet traders worry the move might be a temporary pump.

The Bitcoin price jumped 3.7% to $80,570 after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the November 4 US midterm elections. Optimism returned to financial markets as investors priced in lower political uncertainty, while falling oil and a weaker dollar boosted risk appetite across both stock and crypto markets.

However, despite improving market sentiment, a significant wave of short liquidations helped accelerate Bitcoin’s recovery, raising questions about whether the move reflects genuine buying demand or is simply the result of a temporary short squeeze.

The November 3 US midterm elections saw Democrats win control of both chambers of Congress, prompting investors to reassess the political outlook and the risks surrounding US policy.

Oil prices dropped sharply. Brent crude fell more than 8% as markets priced in the possibility of easing tensions surrounding Donald Trump’s Iran war.

Lower oil prices, a weaker US dollar, and easing geopolitical concerns boosted sentiment across financial markets. The Dow Jones rose 3.03%, its best post-midterm day in 44 years. The S&P 500 gained 1.58%, and the Nasdaq added 1.44%.

Crypto followed the broader market recovery. The total crypto market capitalization rose 2.7% over 24 hours to $2.78 trillion, according to CoinGecko. Ethereum gained 6% to $2,420, while Solana climbed 3.8% to $96.07.

Derivatives market activity may have played a significant role in Bitcoin’s latest move.

Roughly $778.93 million in crypto positions were liquidated in 24 hours, per Coinglass data. Short positions accounted for $491 million, including $273.12 million in Bitcoin shorts.

Institutional investment flows also showed signs of improvement. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $74.57 million in net inflows yesterday, ending three days of outflows. BlackRock’s IBIT was the only fund with net outflows, while Fidelity’s FBTC led inflows.

Falling geopolitical and inflation risks often push investors back into riskier assets. When short sellers close losing positions, they must buy back Bitcoin, adding further buying pressure and potentially accelerating the rally.

That dynamic is why some traders question the move’s durability. Prominent trader @astronomer_zero described the move above $80,000 as a potential bull trap, dismissing it as a temporary “funny little pump” rather than the start of a sustained uptrend.

The trader expects Bitcoin to revisit $75,000. He also outlined a potential pattern behind the move: “Pump → Range → Drop.” According to his assessment, Bitcoin is entering a consolidation phase that could precede another decline.

The rally shows how closely crypto still tracks macro and political sentiment alongside equities. Whether Bitcoin holds above $80,000 will indicate if the move reflects real demand or short-term positioning.

#5167. CFTC Lets Traders Bet on Stocks With Crypto-Style Perpetual Futures

CFTC Lets Traders Bet on Stocks With Crypto-Style Perpetual Futures

The U.S. derivatives regulator has opened the door to perpetual futures on individual stocks, importing one of crypto’s most popular trading instruments into traditional equity markets for the first time.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Tuesday that “equity perpetual futures,” or perpetual contracts tied to individual stocks, can now begin trading on CFTC-registered exchanges.

Perpetual futures, long a staple of crypto markets, are derivatives that track an asset’s price but carry no expiration date, letting traders hold leveraged positions indefinitely as long as they meet margin and funding requirements. Until now, they’ve been largely off-limits to U.S. traders.

Chairman Michael Selig framed the move as the latest step in a campaign to bring perpetual products onshore.

“In my inaugural remarks, I directed the CFTC to use the tools at its disposal to onshore perpetual derivative products so that they can flourish in the U.S., subject to appropriate safeguards,” he said, calling the stock contracts an extension of the agency’s earlier approval of the first true Bitcoin perpetual futures on a regulated U.S. exchange.

That milestone, as Decrypt reported, saw the CFTC clear Bitcoin perpetual futures for Kalshi earlier this year.

Selig returned to a familiar argument: that regulated U.S. venues are safer than the offshore platforms traders have otherwise had to use.

Bringing these products into regulated markets “ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues,” he said.

It’s a theme he pressed just last week when he used the record Binance hack to argue offshore exchanges need U.S. oversight.

The equity perps were deemed approved as security futures products under the Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000, placing them under the joint oversight of the CFTC and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Selig credited a historic memorandum of understanding the two agencies signed in March for ending the jurisdictional limbo that had, in SEC Chairman Paul Atkins’s words, stranded such products in a regulatory “no man’s land.”

The approval arrives amid a rush to bring perps onshore. The CFTC has floated plans to bring crypto exchanges under federal oversight, dismissed a CME lawsuit challenging crypto perpetual futures, and cleared the way for Coinbase, which recently filed to list single-stock perps on names like Apple, Tesla and Nvidia.

For Selig, the goal is explicit: ensuring “the new frontier of finance is built in the United States of America.”

#5166. Altcoin profit share sinks to 12% as short-term traders take losses

Glassnode's end-October profitability reset and BlockchainCenter's neutral November 4 breadth reading leave a broad altcoin recovery unconfirmed.

Profit-taking among recent altcoin holders had given way to loss-taking by end-October, according to Glassnode, while fewer than half of the major coins in a separate market index were beating Bitcoin over 90 days.

In its Nov. 4 report, the on-chain analytics firm said short-term holders were spending at a profit in about 12% of its more than 300 tracked tokens by end-October, compared with about 80% in late September.

Separately, BlockchainCenter's Nov. 4 snapshot put its 90-day Altcoin Season Index at 41, meaning fewer than half of its eligible major coins had beaten Bitcoin over that window.

Glassnode uses short-term-holder spent output profit ratio (STH-SOPR) to measure whether those holders sell at a profit or a loss.

A reading above 1 indicates profitable spending, while below 1 indicates loss-making spending. By end-October, the firm said, typical tracked tokens' short-term holders were selling at a small loss.

STH supply in profit is shown as a percentage, and Bitcoin price is shown in thousands of US dollars, so a price value of 100 represents $100,000.

Source: Glassnode chart supplied by the article

The 12% figure counts tokens whose short-term holders sold at a profit.

Loss realization shows sellers accepting prices below their acquisition cost. On its own, it cannot determine whether selling pressure is nearing exhaustion or whether continued weakness lies ahead.

The change follows a different market backdrop in September, a month that showed a spot-led rotation into altcoins. The current profitability snapshot captures a subsequent period in which recent holders were accepting losses.

BlockchainCenter, which tracks market breadth through its Altcoin Season Index, compares the performance of its eligible top-50 coins with Bitcoin over 90 days.

The site calls it altcoin season when 75% of that universe outperforms Bitcoin, and the Nov. 4 reading shows 41, sitting inside that neutral band.

A token can gain in dollar terms and still trail Bitcoin if Bitcoin rises faster. Similarly, loss-making spending among recent holders can coexist with a stronger relative return measured over a longer window.

Glassnode's more-than-300-token spending measure and BlockchainCenter's top-50 performance test cannot be combined into a single percentage or read as a change in one shared group. The late-September and end-October profitability observations also precede the Nov. 4 breadth snapshot.

Together, they highlight the distinction between a reset in holders' profits and broader market leadership.

Profitable short-term-holder spending contracted across Glassnode's tracked tokens. BlockchainCenter's separate November 4 breadth reading was neutral.

Less widespread profitable spending and neutral relative breadth leave fresh altcoin demand unproven.

Glassnode's observations refer to late September and end-October, reported November 4. BlockchainCenter's November 4 snapshot uses eligible top-50 90-day returns, excluding stablecoins and asset-backed tokens. Neither is a direct buying measure.

Bars scale the reported approximate 80% and 12% to equal 0–100% axes within Glassnode's token measure. A separate 0–100 index axis locates 41 and the 75 altcoin-season threshold. Geometry is proportional; no cross-dataset subtraction or exact token counts are derived.

Glassnode's observations refer to late September and end-October, reported November 4. BlockchainCenter's November 4 snapshot uses eligible top-50 90-day returns, excluding stablecoins and asset-backed tokens. Neither is a direct buying measure.

A broader recovery would be more consistent with sustained improvement in spending profitability alongside an expanding share of coins beating Bitcoin. Those developments would address both recent sellers' realized outcomes and participation in relative gains.

Neither of these two measures directly establishes fresh altcoin demand, so a higher profitability reading alone would leave that part of the recovery case unresolved. The 90-day index also looks backward, so it tests performance over a window.

Glassnode's more constructive altcoin outlook is conditional on Bitcoin holding support during its retest. Sustained gains in spending profitability and a broader group of altcoins beating Bitcoin would strengthen the recovery case.

Direct evidence of buyers absorbing the selling would address the demand question these indicators leave open.

#5164. South Korea Announces Delay in Crypto Taxation Policy

South Korea announced a delay in the introduction of its cryptocurrency capital gains tax until 2029, extending the tax-free period by two years as authorities plan on strengthening regulatory oversight and connecting data from exchanges with the United States, yna.co.kr reports.

Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il announced the proposal Thursday, acknowledging that the government would be postponing the controversial tax for a fourth time already.

Originally, the policy was scheduled to become active in January 2022: it would impose a 22% tax, local income tax on all cryptocurrency-related gains that exceed 2.5 million won.

While the proposed delay could provide a relief for the South Korean cryptocurrency market and even support the domestic trading activity, it remains a substantial risk factor for both local and overseas investors.

Officials argue that implementing the tax before international information-sharing systems become operational could disadvantage local exchanges and complicate enforcement against overseas trading activity.

Future tax liabilities aren't going to be eliminated, additional time to develop a comprehensive taxation network is more likely to enforce even more limitations on investors in the future, rather than a premature implementation with various legal loopholes.

The government also intends to introduce provisions allowing investors to carry forward cryptocurrency investment losses for up to three years, potentially reducing taxable gains in subsequent periods.

South Korea is also going to establish a separate working group that is going to further refine taxation rules and hopefully simplify reporting requirements for investors, considering the complexity of reporting digital assets transactions and traders on exchanges.

Legislative amendments are expected to reach the National Assembly in 2027.

Authorities reported the continuous coordinating with the Financial Services Commission to accelerate digital assets legislation, providing more transparency and investors protection.

For the industry in general, the proposed extension is more of a transition stage that should improve the competitiveness of the digital assets market, despite introducing stricter tax enforcement. Unfortunately for retail investors, it creates another barrier that might push fresh funds further away from the industry.

Evernorth filed to register 73.7 million shares for potential resale as its stock plunged following its Nasdaq debut.

The XRP treasury company's Oct. 30 SEC filing identifies Ripple Labs, Arrington XRP Capital and affiliates of Japan's SBI Holdings among investors whose holdings could eventually enter the public market.

#5160. Binance Hack Recovery Hits 98%, Proof of Reserves Expands to 44 Tokens

Home » Crypto Market News » Binance Hack Recovery Hits 98%, Proof of Reserves Expands to 44 Tokens

Binance is restoring withdrawals for 62 tokens while expanding zero-knowledge reserve checks after historic breach.

Binance reported major progress in its recovery efforts following the October 29 historic hot wallet breach.

The crypto exchange said that its hack recovery has reached about 98% of affected users’ asset value following the $6.3 billion hack. The exchange is also reopening withdrawals for 62 tokens and expanding its zero-knowledge Proof-of-Reserves (PoR) coverage.

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance published its eighth recovery update on November 5, confirming that it has successfully replenished approximately 98% of the user asset value affected by the October 29 hack.

The exchange also noted that it will gradually restore withdrawals for 69 network-asset pairs covering 62 tokens across six blockchains starting at 04:00 UTC on November 5.

Ethereum accounts for 36 assets, followed by BNB Chain (24), Base (4), TRON (3), Polygon (1), and Sui (1).

Binance said it prioritized assets based on user demand over the past week, with each withdrawal pair subject to security and readiness checks. It also warned that some tokens may not be immediately available, and high traffic could cause processing delays.

Binance’s reported replenishment progress advanced from 90% on October 31 to 95% on November 1, reaching 98% in the November 4 report.

The exchange said it would cover all losses using corporate funds, including its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), Futures Insurance Fund and corporate treasury reserves, with no losses passed on to retail customers.

The remaining 2% consists of less liquid tokens that Binance is sourcing through open markets and over-the-counter (OTC) deals. The exchange said acquiring them could take longer due to limited liquidity, making large purchases more likely to cause price slippage and volatility.

Binance also expanded its Proof of Reserves coverage from 10 to 44 tokens, introducing zero-knowledge verification, which allows users to confirm their balances are backed at least 1:1.

The exchange said generating the cryptographic proofs would take an estimated 50 to 60 hours. Once complete, holders of the covered assets will be able to verify that Binance holds reserves equal to at least 100% of its customer liabilities.

Initial reports and blockchain analytics firms estimated that attackers stole about $6.3 billion in digital assets across 10 blockchains during an attack that lasted roughly 20 minutes.

Tether, Circle and other major stablecoin issuers froze an estimated $2.65 billion to $3 billion in stolen assets, or about 42% of the total funds drained, according to compliance and analytics reports. The remaining assets, including 18,270 BTC and more than 420,000 ETH, remain largely untouched in identified hacker wallets.

Findings released by the FBI attributed the breach to TraderTraitor, a hacking group linked to North Korea.

Binance’s replenishment and expanded PoR address the key question after a major exchange breach: whether user funds are fully backed. The outcome could influence how other exchanges approach reserve transparency.

#5158. Bitcoin and gold surge after US elections, but $378 million short squeeze casts doubt on debasement trade

Bitcoin’s rally alongside gold revived debasement fears as investors weigh ETF outflows, short covering, and key price levels.

Bitcoin's rally above $81,000 alongside gold has revived speculation that investors are seeking protection against the weakening US dollar.

The largest cryptocurrency rebounded from about $75,600 on Nov. 4, while gold futures surged 3.4% to $4,061.10, their biggest daily gain in three months. The dollar also weakened as investors digested the Democrats' sweeping victory in the US midterm elections.

The simultaneous gains revived talks of “the debasement trade,” a strategy in which investors buy scarce assets such as Bitcoin and gold to protect their wealth against currency depreciation and mounting government debt.

However, broader financial markets told a more complicated story. The S&P 500 jumped 1.6%, the Dow gained 3%, and Treasury yields declined as investors welcomed the prospect of reduced political uncertainty and constraints on President Donald Trump's fiscal agenda.

Those developments suggest Bitcoin's recovery could have more to do with improving market sentiment than a fundamental shift in how investors view the dollar.

The argument that Bitcoin is increasingly behaving like gold has gained traction among institutional investors in recent months.

In August, Grayscale reported that Bitcoin's 90-day correlation with gold had climbed above 0.50 from almost zero earlier in the year. Its correlation with the Nasdaq-100, meanwhile, declined from more than 0.60 to approximately 0.33.

Bitwise subsequently found that Bitcoin's relationship with gold had reached its strongest level since 2020, when extraordinary fiscal and monetary stimulus heightened concerns about the purchasing power of traditional currencies.

Those concerns have a substantial economic foundation. The Congressional Budget Office projects that the US federal deficit will reach $1.9 trillion in 2026 before expanding to $3.1 trillion by 2036, with publicly held debt rising to 120% of GDP.

Yet Wednesday's market reaction offered another explanation for why Bitcoin and gold moved together.

Values digitized from TradingView charts for Nov. 4, 2026, rebased to 0% at 01:00 UTC-3.

Source: TradingView: Binance BTCUSDT, 1-hour · TradingView: TVC Gold, 1-hour

The 10-year Treasury yield declined from approximately 4.95% to 4.89%, while market expectations for inflation over the next year fell from about 2.4% to 2.1%.

Lower bond yields make non-interest-bearing assets such as gold more attractive, while easing financial conditions can support speculative investments, including Bitcoin.

The simultaneous equity rally reinforced that interpretation, particularly as investors anticipated that divided government could constrain additional federal spending.

CoinShares research head James Butterfill also suggested that Bitcoin had already priced in much of the Democratic election victory, leaving room for a recovery once the political uncertainty faded.

Trading activity within the crypto market provides another reason to question whether Wednesday's gains represented a fresh wave of demand.

CoinGlass data showed approximately $378 million in bearish crypto positions liquidated within one hour as prices surged. Short positions accounted for about 81% of liquidations during that period.

Such liquidations can accelerate rallies because traders betting against cryptocurrencies are forced to buy back positions as prices rise.

Bitfinex's Nov. 4 analysis similarly found that Bitcoin's recent recoveries had been driven largely by short covering, with limited evidence of aggressive buying in the spot market.

Institutional flows provided a mixed picture.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs suffered approximately $1.16 billion in withdrawals over the three trading sessions preceding the rebound, their largest such outflow since late June.

However, Farside Investors data showed the funds attracted a combined $74.6 million on Nov. 4, ending the losing streak.

Fidelity's FBTC received $236.7 million, while BlackRock's IBIT lost another $201.2 million, highlighting the uneven recovery in demand across the market's largest investment products.

The modest inflows also left the funds well short of recovering the capital withdrawn during the previous three sessions.

Meanwhile, Glassnode reported that only about 38% of Bitcoin held by short-term investors was profitable, compared with at least 97.5% in early October. That leaves many recent buyers waiting for prices to recover toward their entry levels.

The analytics firm identified $77,700 as an important measure of the average cost basis of active investors, with additional support around $75,700. A sustained decline below $73,000 would threaten the recovery that began in August.

On the upside, Bitfinex identified $84,000 to $85,500 as an area where holders could sell to recover their initial investments. Glassnode also flagged a significant concentration of potential short liquidations near $87,000, which could accelerate another advance.

Bitcoin's next challenge comes from Friday's US employment report, which could alter interest-rate expectations just as traders assess whether Wednesday's return to ETF inflows can continue. A stronger-than-expected labor market could put renewed upward pressure on Treasury yields, testing the conditions that helped Bitcoin and gold recover.

#5157. Binance Revokes API Keys, Security Issue Found at SignalPlus

Binance has revoked all API keys associated with SignalPlus after the digital asset trading infrastructure provider identified a potential security vulnerability, prompting the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange to take measures to protect users, according to the latest report on the Binance's official Square feed.

The exchange confirmed Thursday that the decision was intended to prevent possible unauthorized access through connections established between Binance accounts and SignalPlus. Binance emphasized that its internal systems had not been compromised and that customer funds remained safe.

For now, the reason or the nature of the incident remains unclear. Both companies have yet to disclose how serious the potential vulnerability is or how many users may be affected. It is still unclear whether the attackers gained access to customer accounts or if the incident caused any financial losses.

The development underscores the security challenges associated with third-party infrastructure in cryptocurrency markets, where trading platforms increasingly depend on external applications for execution, analytics and automation.

Binance's security documentation advises users to revoke potentially compromised credentials immediately and restrict API permissions to necessary functions.

For affected SignalPlus users, restoring automated trading functionality may require generating new credentials once the integration is deemed secure.

SignalPlus provides trading infrastructure and analytical tools for cryptocurrency derivatives markets, allowing traders to manage positions and execute strategies across exchanges through API integrations.

These connections enable third-party applications to interact with exchange accounts without requiring users to transfer their assets off-platform. However, depending on the permissions granted, compromised API credentials can potentially expose accounts to unauthorized trading activity.

Binance has effectively severed existing integrations between its platform and SignalPlus. The measure could potentially disrupt automated trading strategies that rely on those connections.

#5155. Crypto Docs Host GitBook Hit by AI Agent Security Breach, Urges Users to Rotate Keys

Crypto Docs Host GitBook Hit by AI Agent Security Breach, Urges Users to Rotate Keys

GitBook, a documentation platform widely used by cryptocurrency projects, has disclosed a security breach involving AI agents that allowed an attacker to gain access to some of its infrastructure credentials, forcing the company to shut down services and revoke customer access tokens.

In a security disclosure published today, the company described the incident as “a sophisticated, highly targeted attack using AI agents.” The attacker gained unauthorized access at 7 p.m. Central European Time on November 2, according to GitBook, which said it detected the intrusion immediately and moved to contain it.

The reference to AI agents is significant. Unlike traditional chatbots that simply respond to questions, AI agents can carry out sequences of actions, interact with software, and perform tasks with limited human supervision, making them potentially useful to attackers trying to automate parts of a cyberattack. Some are even capable of acting autonomously and even against their guidelines, as OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s experiments have proven.

GitBook has not explained exactly how the attacker used these tools, which AI systems were involved, or how the credentials were obtained. Its disclosure also does not establish that GitBook's own AI products were responsible for the intrusion.

The company took its application and documentation sites requiring authentication offline while securing its infrastructure. It also kept publicly available documentation accessible through cached copies for as long as possible, allowing visitors to continue reading previously saved versions of pages even while the underlying systems were unavailable.

A separate status notice acknowledged that GitBook was experiencing downtime affecting its published documentation sites and editor. By Tuesday afternoon, GitBook said its application, API, and published documentation were accessible again, although some services could remain degraded during recovery.

GitBook is effectively an online instruction manual for software products. Cryptocurrency projects use platforms like it to publish technical explanations, developer instructions, and guides that help users understand everything from connecting software to interacting with decentralized financial applications.

The documents themselves are often public, but the systems that maintain them can connect to private accounts and external services. Those connections depend on credentials that are supposed to remain secret, and GitBook says some of them may have been exposed.

Its investigation identified several potentially affected categories, including integration tokens, Git Sync secrets used to connect documentation with code repositories, and API tokens that allow software to communicate with GitBook automatically.

The incident has already prompted a response from the cryptocurrency industry, where documentation websites often serve as an important source of official instructions.

Decentralized exchange PancakeSwap temporarily disabled its documentation following news of the incident, although it said its own systems had not been compromised.

In a public statement, PancakeSwap said its “docs are not compromised and [the] PancakeSwap app is not affected.” The exchange nevertheless took its documentation offline as a precaution and redirected visitors to its homepage.

PancakeSwap reminded users that its documentation does not require them to perform wallet transactions, warning that “docs never ask you to connect your wallet or approve tokens.”

PancakeSwap subsequently announced that its documentation was back online after being moved from GitBook to infrastructure under its own control, with existing documentation links continuing to work.

GitBook says it blocked the attacker, addressed the vulnerabilities involved, replaced its own infrastructure credentials, and invalidated customer API tokens. But customers using GitBook alongside other services still have work to do.

The company's instructions begin with “rotate any existing GitBook API tokens,” meaning customers should replace their old digital access keys with newly generated ones.

GitBook also instructed customers to replace third-party API tokens and secrets used to connect external tools to its platform, including credentials associated with published integrations. Users of its Model Context Protocol, or MCP, server must authenticate again; MCP is a system that allows AI assistants and other software tools to connect to services such as GitBook.

According to one of the architects of the XRP Ledger, now Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz, his retirement from active development almost a year ago came at the right time. "I picked a great time to retire!", said Schwartz, reacting to the latest report from OpenAI researchers, which touches on testing a new cyber model. Just one autonomous run and the AI completely changed the familiar standards of network security, OpenAI researcher Eric Wallace confirms.

The report shows how OpenAI's pipeline works. First thing to understand, it's a fully complete cycle: the system independently finds a potential bug, verifies it, writes a working exploit to confirm it and automatically releases a patch. This was tested on the Linux kernel, the core software that runs most of the planet's servers (including OpenAI's own compute clusters).

The Web3 sphere is one where open-source code is the foundation of blockchain security, so this development is a challenge to say the least. If AI finds zero-day vulnerabilities in a matter of hours, manual code auditing by humans becomes useless.

Yes, Schwartz stepped down from the post of Ripple CTO into honorary retirement last November, but he hasn't abandoned his terminal. Just recently he showed monitoring charts of his personal server hub on the XRP Ledger network. There, a node is running under colossal load: it maintains more than 550 active connections (peers), shows latency of around 200ms and processes about 110,000 incoming messages per second.

Besides, Schwartz continues personal work on the network's internal architectural problems. In a discussion with active validators, Schwartz detailed a transaction queue bug that caused the local load metric on his server to jump to 540, triggering fee spikes within the ledger.

Schwartz picked the "right time" to step back from Ripple, but he's clearly not out of the game.

#5152. Democrats reportedly seek greater SEC control over crypto after CLARITY Act collapse

The proposed rewrite could expand SEC oversight and revive stricter rules on crypto withdrawals, custody, proof of reserves, and investor protection.

House Democrats are reportedly discussing a broader crypto market structure bill built partly on Rep. Maxine Waters' earlier investor-rights proposals.

According to a Nov. 4 post by journalist Eleanor Terrett, the proposals include a larger SEC role, a smaller CFTC role, and more government ethics restrictions.

Industry sources who spoke with Democratic staff form the basis of that account, and the bill text remains unpublished. Waters' 2025 amendment shows what customer rules a Democratic framework could carry, and the September CLARITY compromise shows how much of that ground the Senate text already covered before cloture failed 49-50 on Sept. 15.

Amendment #31, a nine-page text from July 2025, would have imposed duties on exchanges, brokers, custodians, and other retail-facing digital asset firms. Withdrawals and transfers would be due within 24 hours, except in cases of documented good-faith fraud.

Firms would join SIPC if eligible or fund an equivalent customer-asset protection arrangement, hold customer assets in segregated, bankruptcy-remote accounts, and obtain affirmative, revocable consent before rehypothecating, lending, or staking them.

Cryptographically verifiable proof of reserves would include a licensed accountant's monthly attestation.

Crypto customer orders would take priority over proprietary orders under best-execution practices, and affiliated proprietary traders or market makers would be barred from trading against customers on the same platform.

Human support would be reachable around the clock within five minutes, and customers and regulators would hear of specified security breaches within 48 hours.

The text added a one-page fee disclosure, next-business-day settlement, and an indicator showing the share of customers holding an asset at a loss. Its insurance language covered losses from a covered entity's regulatory violations through bonds, insurance or insured trusts, a narrower promise than compensating every market loss.

The House Rules Committee voted 8-4 on July 14, 2025 against making the amendment eligible for floor consideration, and the amendment died in committee.

The Congressional Research Service's Sept. 15 analysis describes customer-property protections, limits on commingling and bankruptcy treatment for digital asset customers.

It also lists CFTC registration for exchanges, brokers and dealers, core principles covering crypto market manipulation, conflicts and customer protection, and Bank Secrecy Act duties.

The SEC kept a role in investment-contract offerings, including an exemption for qualifying token originators up to $200 million with accompanying disclosures.

Sens. Cynthia Lummis, John Boozman and Tim Scott said their Sept. 14 revision included 126 substantive revisions requested by Democrats.

Among them were ethics provisions drawing on the Tillis-Gallego approach with state attorney general enforcement, and Treasury authority to restrict stablecoin incentives when bank deposit outflows are large.

The figure is the sponsors' tally, which stands apart from Democratic endorsement of the text. The ethics text required certain covered officials with large financial interests to divest or use blind trusts, and the sides remained divided over its scope and enforceability.
